title: A diagnostic perturbation can identify susceptibility while contaminating the later trajectory
problem: Estimating a local response gain requires a controlled input. If that input causes a persistent state change, the later output belongs to the post-probe trajectory rather than the original baseline trajectory.
required_before_baseline_like_prediction: predeclared diagnostic challenge magnitude and duration
remeasure the same state proxy after washout
predeclared equivalence margin for residual probe effect
later functional endpoint under probe and sham conditions
pass_rule: The confidence interval for post-washout probe-vs-sham state/output difference lies wholly inside the predeclared equivalence region, with all required controls present.
unknown_rule: Boundary-overlapping uncertainty or missing controls keeps washout/reversibility UNKNOWN.
fail_rule: A persistent effect interval wholly outside the equivalence region rejects use of that challenge as a neutral diagnostic probe for the declared later trajectory.
HF01_implication: M susceptibility can be measured only through an input
a useful susceptibility probe can still be unsuitable for forecasting an untreated baseline-like trajectory
observer back-action and diagnostic-input back-action are separate failure modes and require separate controls
claim_boundary: This contract does not classify DHT, MCH, YODA1 or any other specific perturbation as reversible. Reversibility must be demonstrated for the exact model, dose, timing and endpoint before predictive reuse.
